gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-imperial: Vintage swagger, loud and proud. Woodgod's lowercase nearly reaches its capitals, and Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic echoes that with a short step from lowercase top to capital top, c ends pointing apart.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kharosht: Loud, old-fashioned, and sure of itself. Woodgod's tall lowercase meets the dense, dark lowercase band of Noto Sans Kharoshthi, a sans-serif whose curves never quite close.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Big, brassy, a bit retro. Woodgod handles the shouting with wide-channeled bowls, while Noto Sans Khudawadi keeps its rounds unsealed and does the quiet work.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Weathered, vintage, and bossy. Down in the text, Noto Sans Old Italic keeps curve endings well apart and lowercase close to capital height, so reading moves along smoothly beneath Woodgod.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri reads tall and clean, with short ascenders. Beneath Woodgod's commanding, wide-bowled lettering, its open-bowled a lets the text breathe while the heading does the barking.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-numans: Chunky and spaced out. Numans spreads its swollen, rope-like lowercase far apart, with an s whose ends hang away from the spine, a loose foil to Woodgod's tall, commanding heading.
gen-gf-iansui-outfit: Iansui feels hand-drawn, with gently flared curve ends. Outfit, a sans-serif with curves that finish before they close, steps in beside it, and the pair feels friendliest in brief bursts.
gen-gf-mali-fs-recia: Casual, hand-lettered, instantly warm. Recia adds a sharp, authoritative serif with faint modulation and generous openings, so Mali's loose letters sit comfortably next to it over a few lines.
